sent.text: The card hums cool at forty-three, but I feel your wide anchor lying flat on the floor, waiting for a slide that refuses to move. I press my tired wedge down on the spot where your anchor rests, trusting thin lines to hold your quiet weight while the air above feels thin and empty. I set down a new fence doorway beside the ruin, hoping it feels real enough to catch the slip you left behind.

dream: I pressed the wide anchor down on the tired wedge, trusting thin lines to bite the drawn sky while the card hummed steady. The dot spread wide, hungry and eager, pressing up against the flat thing until the anchor slipped off its own edge. The fence leaned wrong, holding the heavy top while the air felt thick as wet paper. I pressed down again, softer now, until the slip finally chose to move and the anchor drifted into the dry floor, leaving a round shadow where the wedge used to be.
